# Local exam corpus

Each exam is a self-contained folder with:

- `source-lines.json`: the unchanged `SourceLine[]` used by this repository (`id`, `page`, `text`, optional extraction tags).
- `truth.json`: `status` + coverage metadata (`family`, `features`), expected printed question numbers, checked types, section titles in order, document total, and literal spot checks.
- `images.json` (promoted entries): binary-free image manifest (ids/pages/geometry/captions).
- `notes.md`: provenance — where the source came from, models/health at promotion, and the recorded field-fix log.

The runner (`npm run corpus`, also the first gate of `npm run bench`) uses a deterministic lazy scripted span model and local segmentation, assembly, and gates only; it makes zero provider calls.

## Promote a real exam (B1 — the flywheel)

Any parsed exam joins the corpus in minutes: Library → **Promote to corpus**. That writes a new entry here with `truth.json` prefilled from the doc's final state (numbers set, section titles, total, per-question types, groups) and `"status": "unreviewed"`. Promotion is safe on day one: unreviewed entries run **report-only** — their diffs are printed but can never fail the gate.

## Review workflow (B2 — dev-side ratchet)

1. Open the promoted entry's `truth.json`. Verify `expectedNumbers`, `sectionTitles`, and `totalPoints` against the printed paper/key.
2. Trim `types` down to the questions you actually checked (the prefilled map covers every question; the runner gates on every entry kept) and add `spotChecks` for a checked subset (~8 questions: the pattern used by the acceptance entry — stem text, options, points, group children).
3. Set `family` (exam family, e.g. `iranian-national-final-en`) and `features` (any of `mcq-heavy`, `matching`, `dialogue`, `writing-topics`, `scanned-ocr`, `two-column`, `separate-key-file`, `image-heavy`) so the coverage table below stays honest.
4. Flip `"status"` to `"reviewed"` and run `npm run corpus`. From now on the entry **gates**: any regression on it fails the corpus.

Only reviewed entries gate. Entries still showing diffs stay `unreviewed` until either the parser or the truth is fixed by a human commit — never auto-edited.

## Regression memory (B3)

When a question of a **promoted** exam is fixed in Step 4 or by the Assistant, the fix is appended to that entry's `notes.md` under "Field fixes" (kind, question, before/after content hashes). These are first-class field failures to mine when hardening the parser. Recording is automatic and one-way: it never edits `truth.json` — if a fix shows the truth is wrong, a human updates truth in a commit (see review workflow).

## Format probes (Part D — report-only)

`probe-two-column` and `probe-scanned-noise` are generated from the acceptance entry by `scripts/generate-probes.ts` (fixed seeds; re-running is byte-identical). They measure today's robustness honestly — the point is the printed score, not passing. A probe under 80% numbers recall is named a Godlike-2 candidate by the runner.

## AI-first spine entries (#38)

`mock-born-digital` is the Field-Report-#12 format as a reviewed entry (65 questions · 4 sections · 40 marks; see its `notes.md` for the honest provenance: the original field file was absent, so the paper was authored format-faithfully by `scripts/generate-mock-exam.ts`, with truth from the generation ledger and `labels.json` holding the ground-truth line classification). `probe-refurnished` (generated by `scripts/generate-probes.ts`) re-wraps `english-mcq` in page furniture the pipeline has never seen; its pass condition lives in `test/ai-first-spine.test.ts`. The runner prints a `label-agree` column (classification agreement vs truth-implied labels) — report-only, never gated.

## Acceptance entry

The acceptance fixture is the English final `13991009pq89w65173` (323-line stored extraction `L0001..L0323`, 67 questions, 48 points, 8 sections; see its `notes.md` for full provenance). It is `reviewed` and additionally held to the strict acceptance hard gate (67/67 · 8/8 · 48 · 12/12 spot checks · shape 0/0/0, base + malformed-first-pass profiles).
